text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS

- Farmers will stage a three-day demonstration from today by again blocking road lanes in 200 places in several counties and the capital to enforce their demands that their tax and social insurance burdens be lowered. @

- The Belgian news agency Saturday quoted a NATO diplomat as saying it is conceivable that only the Czech Republic and Poland will be admitted to NATO in the first round, while Hungary will be relegated to the second round for political reasons.
- Workers at the power plant Matrai Eromu have threatened to stage a two-hour warning strike on Wednesday and a full-blown strike from February 27.
- Police checked over 4,500 cars and caught 15 persons in two Budapest car markets on Sunday and found eight stolen cars.
NEPSZABADSAG @
- German President Roman Herzog begins a three-day official visit to Hungary starting Tuesday, when he will address Parliament.
VILAGGAZDASAG

- Sandor Puskas, president of the supervisory board of the State Privatisation and Holding Co., submitted his resignation on Friday after committee members requested him to do so. Puskas is now implicated in the Tocsik affair. @
- Prime Minister Gyula Horn and Budapest Mayor Gabor Demszky announced Friday that the construction of a fourth underground line in Budapest could start in the second half of 1998.

- The foreign trade balance deteriorated by $230 million last year, mainly due to a higher than expected increase in imports, the Central Statistics Office reported. More positively, the tourism surplus double to $1.3 billion, bringing the current account deficit down to $1.7 billion.
MAGYAR HIRLAP @
- Russia's ultrantionalist Liberal Democratic Party, headed by Vladimir Zhirinovsky, will stage a demonstration outside the Hungarian Embassy in Moscow today against the planned enlargement of NATO.

- Finance Minister Peter Medgyessy said court proceedings could be launched against GE Capital, if it can be proved that the former owner of Polgari Bank was negligent while the bank accumulated losses of HUF 1 billion last year. An unidentified GEC official called the announcement unjust. @
- Hungary and the International Organisation for Migration will assist the voluntary return home of refugees staying in Hungary, according to a cooperation agreement.
- Hungary's population declined by 38,000 last year.
NAPI GAZDASAG
- Savings cooperatives lent HUF 2.866 billion to agricultural enterprises last year.
- The state agricultural concern Babolna closed 1996 with pre-tax profits of HUF 1.5 billion on sales of HUF 67 billion. @
- The Friday AGM of Hungary's largest steel group Dunaferr approved the 1997 business plan, projecting pre-tax profits of HUF 7.3 billion on net sales of HUF 188 billion.

- Pannonia Hotels Rt. closed very successful 1996 with pre-tax profits of HUF 1.9 billion from domestic hotels, HUF 80 million from units in Austria, but losses of HUF 150 million incurred by hotels in Germany.
- The insurance company Hungaria Biztosito is willing to participate in the privatisation of Takarekbank along with a strategic investor.
